title: feat(automation): a paused screen says whether another screen follows, and the flow runner reads Next or Submit and counts steps
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBGT99SR6FyoGywxafVEzdB1)_

Fixes #26657

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:屏幕流暂停时,引擎按流程图在 `ScreenSpec.progress` 里说明「后面还有没有屏幕」(`none` / `possible` / `certain`),只有在每条路径都一致时才附带第几步、共几步;Console 的 `FlowRunner` 据此把按钮写成「下一步」或「提交」,并且只在总数确定时画「第 N 步,共 M 步」。
- **为什么改**:hotcrm 的发起合同向导每一步按钮都是「提交」,申请人在第 1 步就以为合同已经提交;也画不出步数,因为暂停的屏幕里没有这些信息,而流程在任何屏幕之后都可能分支,只有引擎知道。
- **风险与回滚**:契约只加一个可选成员,旧服务端不发它,旧客户端忽略它;没有 `progress` 时按钮照旧是「提交」。引擎侧只在屏幕暂停时读一次流程图。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts` 的 `readScreenProgress`(分支、环、扇出与子流程的判定),`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` 的 `ScreenProgressSpec`,`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx` 的按钮与计步。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/builtin/screen-progress.test.ts`,预期 13 个测试全绿(线性、分支、环、审批式暂停、子流程各有一条)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地(需先过契约档复核)。

## What changes

**The shape: `ScreenSpec.progress?: ScreenProgressSpec`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, with its wire spelling on `TriggerFlowResponseSchema` in `api/automation-api.zod.ts`, bound to the interface by the existing compile-time identity pin):

```ts
interface ScreenProgressSpec {
  nextScreen: 'none' | 'possible' | 'certain';
  step?: number;       // 1-based, only when every path from the start agrees
  stepCount?: number;  // only alongside step, when every path through this screen agrees
}
```

Why this shape:
- **A tri-state, not a boolean.** A flow can branch after any screen. A boolean `isLast` would have to guess on a branch: `false` claims more screens follow when they may not, `true` claims the end when one may follow. `'possible'` says exactly what the graph knows. The runner reads both `'possible'` and `'certain'` as "Next", because a later screen can still come; `'certain'` stays distinct so a reader can tell the two apart without walking the graph.
- **The counts are optional members of the same object, each present only when exact.** "Absent" means "the graph does not make it exact", never "zero" or "unknown server". The whole object is absent only when the engine cannot answer at all (a server that predates it, or the child-run case below), and a runner then keeps its old label.
- **One nested member, not three flat ones on `ScreenSpec`.** The three come from one computation and mean nothing apart; one optional key keeps the "no answer" state a single check.
- **A served fact, not an authorable key.** Nothing a metadata author writes changes (`Metadata-protocol: none`); no author can mis-declare it.

**The engine fills it** (`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts`, `readScreenProgress`), reading the graph of the flow the run executes at the moment a `screen` pauses:
- Every out-edge is a way the run may go; conditions are not evaluated ahead of time. `nextScreen` is plain reachability for `'none'`, and the fewest surely-pausing screens on any path to a point where the run may stop (a 0-1 BFS) for `'certain'`.
- **A branch after a screen answers `'possible'`** — a `decision` with a branch that pauses on another screen and one that does not, a fault edge, a loop back. The engine never picks a branch.
- `step` / `stepCount` are computed over strongly connected components, as the SET of screen totals the paths give; a count is served only when that set has one member. A loop through a screen, a parallel fan-out (several unconditional successors, an inclusive decision), a `subflow`, or a screen the caller may already have answered makes the count vary, so it is left out.
- What counts as a screen: a `screen` node that surely pauses (an `objectName`, `waitForInput: true`, or declared fields without `waitForInput: false`), the executor's own rule. A field-less pass-through screen is not counted. A screen whose fields the caller supplied (`judgeHeadlessScreen`) may not pause, so it is "maybe". A non-screen node that can pause (an approval, a wait) serves no screen (only a `screen` node sets `NodeExecutionResult.screen`), so the stretch of screens may end there: a screen behind one is possible, never certain.
- **A `subflow`** may serve screens of its child, or none, so the screen before one answers `'possible'` with no total. A screen INSIDE a child run sees only the child graph: it keeps `nextScreen` when that graph shows another screen, and serves no `progress` when it does not, because the parent may continue with screens of its own.

**The runner reads it** (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx`): the flat step's primary button reads `common.next` while `nextScreen` is `'certain'` or `'possible'` and `common.submit` on `'none'` or with no `progress`; the step counter (`form.stepOf`, the wording the form wizard already uses) is drawn beside the flow's name only when both `step` and `stepCount` are served. The `object-form` step's own button (`flowRunner.saveAndContinue`) is the form's and is unchanged.

**Docs:** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` gains "A paused screen says whether another one follows — Next, Submit and the step counter", with the authoring advice that follows from it (keep a wizard's screens on one straight path and branch after the last to get an exact counter).

## Tests

- New `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-progress.test.ts` (13 pins). End to end through the engine: a linear three-screen wizard (`certain 1/3`, `certain 2/3`, `none 3/3`, then completes); an object-form step (`none 1/1`); a branched flow (`possible`, step 1, no total; past the branch `none 2/2`); a looped flow (`certain` then `possible`, no counts, and `certain` again after looping back); a pause that serves no screen (`none 1/1` before an end, `possible` before a screen); a pass-through screen not counted; a subflow (`possible` before it; the child's first screen `certain` with no counts; the child's last screen with no `progress`). Over `readScreenProgress` directly: parallel fan-out, fault paths, a caller-answered screen, an inclusive decision, no start node and an unknown node.
- `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.test.ts`: the trigger response keeps `progress`, and refuses a `nextScreen` outside the closed set, a missing `nextScreen`, `step: 0` and a fractional step.
- New `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/FlowRunner.stepProgress-26657.test.tsx` (6 pins): Next and "Step 1 of 3" on `certain`; Next and no counter on `possible` with no total; Submit and "Step 3 of 3" on `none`; Submit and no counter with no `progress`; a resume that pauses again relabels from the next screen; in zh the words are 下一步 / 提交 / 第 1 步，共 2 步.

## Acceptance notes

- **No new translation keys.** The runner reuses `common.next`, `common.submit` and `form.stepOf`, which every one of the ten bundles already carries (zh: 下一步 / 提交 / 第 {{current}} 步，共 {{total}} 步), so each `defaultValue` equals its `en` value.
- **Skills half owed, not written here.** `skills/**` is a Tier H governed surface; teaching the screen row of `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` (and an eval) in this PR would make the whole PR Tier H. The docs half is here. The seat files the skills follow-up card.
- **File surface beyond the claim, all part of the same contract change:** the wire spelling in `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts` (the existing `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` identity pin reds without it), its test, the docs page, and three regenerated spec artifacts (`api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json`, the `api/` strictness count 446 → 447 for the new module-local `z.object`).
- The engine reads the graph by the run's `flowName` from the engine's flow map (`getFlow`), the same map a run starts and resumes from, and checks the node is a `screen` in it before answering.
- The object-form step's button still reads "Save & Continue" on its last step too; the signal now exists, but relabelling the form's own button is outside this card.
